newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Henry Walker says has A$200 mln contract.
newsitem.headline: Henry Walker says has A$200 mln contract.

text.p: Contract miner and engineer Henry Walker Group Ltd said on Monday it had boosted its iron ore contract mining portfolio with a A$200 million contract at Savage River in Tasmania.
The contract with Australian Bulk Minerals provides takes the value of its work in hand to more than A$1 billion, Henry Walker said in a statement.
Henry Walker said the contract would allow it to conduct mining for 10-1/2 years, with production expected to start by the end of the third quarter.
The company expects the contract will require capital expenditure of A$12 million in the year to June 30, 1998.
The Savage River contract brings the value of the company's work on hand at June 30, 1997, to A$1.01 billion, a 22 percent increase on last year.
Short-term work on hand had also improved, to A$300 million at June 30, 1997, from A$275 million at June 30, 1996, the company said,
New business includes civil engineering contracts worth A$40 million in Australia and Indonesia.
The company has been awarded a A$13.3 million road construction project by Main Roads Western Australia for reconstruction of a section of the Albany Highway.
Henry Walker's Indonesian subsidiary, PT Darma Henwa, has also been awarded a US$19 million joint venture contract with PT Thiess Indonesia.
The joint venture contract is for the construction of a concentrator site and tailings pipeline at the Batu Hijau copper and gold mine on Sumbawa island.
"The new contracts are particularly pleasing in a number of respects," managing director Richard Ryan said in a statement.

"The Savage River contract adds to the large amount of work we have conducted in iron ore mining through our contract with BHP ... at Yandi, and that which we have completed at Mt Tom Price and Koolan Island," he said.
